points.t: A small painful crusted nodule on the helix or antihelix, worse lying on that side, in an older adult.
Pressure on cartilage with poor blood supply leads to inflammation and cartilage damage.
Pressure-relief pillow or ring for 4–6 weeks; consider a potent topical steroid; refer if failing or atypical.
SCC or BCC of the ear (biopsy if not settling), keratoacanthoma (rapid crater), tophaceous gout.

points: A firm, round, 4–10 mm nodule with a **central crust, scale or keratin plug**, sometimes ulcerated.
**Exquisitely tender**: it wakes the patient at night when they lie on it, and **light squeezing causes disproportionate pain** (the course bedside test). Usually on the side the patient sleeps on.
atypical features (rapid growth, bleeding, induration, a size >1 cm, a rolled pearly edge, no pain); no improvement after **6–8 weeks of strict offloading**; immunosuppression; or patient anxiety.
Clinical: site + pain + central crust + sleeping history.
Dermoscopy: central white-yellow keratin/ulcer with a radiating whitish "starburst" and peripheral dotted or linear vessels. It is **non-specific** and **cannot reliably exclude SCC/BCC**.

items.t: Rapidly growing, ulcerating or bleeding ear nodule, or an ear nodule with a nearby lymph node: **suspected SCC**, suspected-cancer referral (NICE NG12).

pearls.t: [Case 2](condition:seborrhoeic-keratosis) medicines: aspirin is relevant only if a biopsy or excision is done. **Do not stop aspirin for minor skin surgery** (BSDS 2023; see the [skin surgery](condition:skin-surgery-preop) notes). Losartan and simvastatin are not causative.
Explain the mechanism ("a pressure sore of the ear cartilage"). Adherence to offloading for at least a month is the key to success.
**Painless** ear nodule plus rapid growth means think SCC/KA. **Very painful at night** means think CNH. But both can coexist, which is why non-resolving CNH gets a biopsy.
Check transplant or immunosuppressant history (azathioprine, ciclosporin, tacrolimus): cSCC risk rises up to 65–100× in organ transplant recipients.
